fixes.explanation: Verse 19 says the scattered believers were speaking the message only to Jews. Then these men from Cyprus and Cyrene get to Antioch and start speaking to the Greeks as well. That's a real change in who hears it. I think those Greeks were glad to hear it.

Egyptians don't turn up in this passage at all, friend. The men from Cyprus and Cyrene go to Antioch and begin speaking to the Greeks as well. Verse 19 says those scattered by the persecution had been speaking the message only to Jews. So the new audience is the Greeks, and that's the news of the day.

"The law was given through Moses" (John 1:17), but that's not what verse 20 says these men bring. The text says they were proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus. That's the message they carried into Antioch. Keep your eyes on that phrase.

Isaiah saw a vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1), and his words matter. But Acts 11:20 doesn't say these men were bringing them to Antioch. What it says is that they were proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus. That's the message on the table here.

Not a handful, friend. Acts 11:21 says a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord. A handful would've been a nice little group, but the text says great number. The same verse says the hand of the Lord was with them.
Not quite, friend. Acts 11:23 says that when Barnabas arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced. Barnabas, the man the Jerusalem church sent, isn't troubled. He's glad.

Damascus isn't where this verse ends up, friend. Acts 11:26 says that when Barnabas found Saul, he brought him back to Antioch. For a full year the two of them met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. So the answer is Antioch.

Nice try, but Nazarenes didn't make it into this verse. Acts 11:26 says, "The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch." Not Nazarenes, but Christians. Antioch is where that name shows up first.
Verse 29 says the disciples decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea. Each one gave according to his ability. That's a kind way to spend a decision.

Samaria never shows up in these verses, friend. The disciples in Antioch decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea (Acts 11:29). Then they sent their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul (Acts 11:30). So the gifts travel to Judea.
